tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here to understand what model-loader does: a Bubble Tea TUI for managing llama-server profiles and processes. The README outlines the five tabs, key features like instance recovery and schema-driven validation, and how to build and run the application.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: This is the primary CLI entry point that dispatches subcommands such as TUI, serve, import, download, and benchmark. It bootstraps the Bubble Tea program with all five tabs, giving you a bird's-eye view of how the application initializes and routes to different modes.
tour.languageLesson: Go's main package convention places the executable entry point in cmd/<binary>/main.go. Subcommands are typically dispatched with a switch on os.Args or a lightweight flag parser before handing off to domain-specific runners.

tour.title: Build Foundation
tour.description: The Go module manifest declares Go 1.26.2 and Charmbracelet TUI dependencies, while the Makefile automates the build, install, and test workflows. Together they define the project's toolchain and external ecosystem.

tour.title: Configuration Layer
tour.description: This file loads the TOML configuration via Viper, defining paths for profiles, state, and logs. It provides the runtime settings that all downstream services rely on, such as the profiles directory and backend catalog location.
tour.languageLesson: Viper is a popular Go configuration library that supports multiple formats including TOML, YAML, and JSON. It uses mapstructure tags to map nested config keys onto struct fields, allowing environment-aware defaults.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: These files define the core vocabulary of the system: BackendKind, Profile, and FlagSchema. With the highest fan-in in the codebase, backend.go is the universal dependency that ties together the catalog, validation, and UI layers. The flag schema establishes the type system for llama-server command-line flags.
tour.languageLesson: Go domain layers typically use plain structs and string-based enums (via typed constants) rather than classes. The lack of inheritance encourages composition through struct embedding and interface satisfaction.

tour.title: Backend Catalog and Schema
tour.description: The backend catalog manages multiple llama-server forks and versions, while the schema generator orchestrates per-backend validation schemas. The Backends tab UI exposes this catalog to the user, allowing selection and configuration of which backend a profile targets.
tour.languageLesson: Go services often separate 'catalog' (discovery and metadata) from 'schema' (validation rules). This decoupling lets the UI consume a stable catalog API while the schema layer evolves independently as backend binaries change.

tour.title: Profile Persistence
tour.description: The profile store provides filesystem-based CRUD for launch profiles, including import and export for sharing configurations. It persists profiles as individual files in a configurable directory, making them portable and version-control friendly.
tour.languageLesson: Filesystem stores in Go often use atomic write patterns (write to temp, then rename) to prevent corruption on crash. The store interface abstracts the FS implementation, allowing test doubles and future migration to other backends.

tour.title: Process Lifecycle
tour.description: The process manager handles launching, monitoring, and recovering llama-server instances. Background instances survive TUI exit and are restored on restart via an instances.json state file. The args builder translates a profile into the exact command-line arguments for the target backend.
tour.languageLesson: Go process management uses os/exec for spawning and syscall for signal handling. Orphaning processes intentionally (so they survive parent death) is done by setting SysProcAttr.Setpgid and avoiding wait calls in the parent.

tour.title: Flag Validation
tour.description: The llamahelp parser extracts flag metadata from llama-server --help output, producing a structured schema pinned to a specific binary version. The validator uses this schema to enforce type correctness, required flags, and backend-specific constraints before launch.
tour.languageLesson: Embedding golden test fixtures (like testdata/help-v7376.golden.json) lets you parse against a known schema when the binary is unavailable. Go's embed directive compiles these files into the binary as static assets.

tour.title: TUI Framework
tour.description: The root model orchestrates the five-tab Bubble Tea application, routing keyboard input and managing global state. The theme layout defines shared dimensions and styling, while reusable components like confirm dialogs are composed across multiple pages.
tour.languageLesson: Bubble Tea follows the Elm architecture: a Model holds state, an Update function handles messages, and a View function renders. Each page implements this trio, and the root model switches between them based on tab selection.

tour.title: Profile Editor
tour.description: The Profiles tab is the heart of the application, listing all profiles and launching the editor. The editor uses Charmbracelet's huh forms with a curated essential-fields registry and an advanced args editor. The essentials registry maps per-backend flags to user-friendly form inputs.
tour.languageLesson: The essentials registry is a curated UX layer, not a generic form abstraction. It uses a map[domain.BackendKind][]EssentialField to control which flags get prominent UI treatment, separating user experience concerns from the underlying argument list.

tour.title: Model Browser
tour.description: The Models tab scans configured directories for .gguf files and extracts metadata such as parameter count, quantization, and context size. The GGUF scanner reads the binary format's header and key-value sections, turning raw files into structured model cards the UI can browse and select.
tour.languageLesson: GGUF is a binary format with a header followed by key-value metadata and tensor info. Go scanners use encoding/binary with explicit byte-order readers to parse platform-independent file formats without reflection overhead.

tour.title: Server Monitor and Benchmark
tour.description: The Server tab shows live logs, health status, GPU metrics, and slot usage for running instances. The HTTP proxy provides an OpenAI-compatible reverse proxy to the underlying llama-server. The Benchmark tab runs evaluation workloads such as SWE-bench Lite and long-context needle probes, storing results per profile.
tour.languageLesson: OpenAI-shaped proxies in Go typically use httputil.ReverseProxy with custom transport and request rewriting. The proxy translates between the OpenAI chat-completion JSON schema and llama-server's native HTTP endpoints, letting existing clients connect without modification.
